Mistake list is sound; no elo tiers present

edits.before: Aurelion Sol wins by landing Astral Flight, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Aurelion Sol wins by kiting with Astral Flight and stacking Stardust — every safe beam second makes the next one worse.

edits.before: - Aurelion Sol Astral Flight: matchup-defining — His reposition and escape — he is a stationary battery while it is down. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Sanguine Pool has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Aurelion Sol Astral Flight (W): 22s at rank 1, matchup-defining — his reposition and escape; he is a stationary battery while it is down. - His R: 120/110/100s, E Singularity 12s. - Your W Sanguine Pool has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R: the moment it goes right.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, E-charge as he steps to answer, release and walk — the trade costs him HP and pays yours.
edits.after: His W Astral Flight is 22s at rank 1 — once he lands, Q-E the stationary battery and walk before his beam adds up.

edits.before: Pooling his poke and then eating the real engage at half HP with nothing — the pool is a combo-breaker, not a flinch reflex.
edits.after: At half HP inside his beam and Singularity range with pool down, the black hole's center executes — back off and reset first.

edits.before: Still surviving. Q on cooldown when free, pool saved for the jungler you haven't seen yet.
edits.after: Still surviving his 750-range beam — Q when free, pool saved for the jungler you haven't seen.

edits.before: E charges join the pattern: Q-E wave contact trades start mattering. Health is your mana — spend like an accountant.
edits.after: His extended Q beam still out-trades your unstacked rotation — E charges join the pattern, spend health carefully.

edits.before: The crimson rush timing — Q empowers every third-ish cast and the sustain war starts tilting your way.
edits.after: Crimson Rush timing — your Q+E sustain now outheals his 3s Q chip and you shove him off his stack farm.

edits.before: Hemoplague online — the all-in inverts: Q-E-R-E with ignite kills most mids who thought they were winning.
edits.after: Hemoplague online — pool his Falling Star stun and the all-in is clean; he has no escape once W is down.

edits.before: Riftmaker timing: every trade heals more than it costs. Extended fights are now donations to your health bar.
edits.after: Riftmaker timing: your sustain out-damages his stack-scaling Q before he powers up — extended trades refund you.

edits.before: Late Vlad is a raid boss: pool their engage, R their clump, and drain whatever stayed to argue.
edits.after: Late Vlad is a raid boss: pool his star, R the clump, and drain whatever stayed to argue.
